scripted_findings.title: 8 page(s) serve an essentially empty HTML shell
scripted_findings.evidence: https://supercell.com/404: 27 words of extractable text, mount element #__next; https://supercell.com/clashofclans-gift: 3 words of extractable text, mount element #__next; https://supercell.com/brawlstars-gift: 3 words of extractable text, mount element #__next; https://supercell.com/clashroyale-gift: 3 words of extractable text, mount element #__next

scripted_findings.title: Brand identity is not anchored to any external profile
scripted_findings.evidence: None of the 11 crawled page(s) declares Organization, LocalBusiness or similar structured data with sameAs links. Without sameAs, an assistant has nothing distinguishing this brand from others sharing the name, which is the standard cause of mistaken identity.

scripted_findings.title: Missing, generic or duplicated <title> on 4 page(s)
scripted_findings.evidence: https://supercell.com/clashofclans-gift: no <title>; https://supercell.com/brawlstars-gift: no <title>; https://supercell.com/clashroyale-gift: no <title>; https://supercell.com/hayday-gift: no <title>. The title is the first thing an index stores and the label an assistant shows next to a citation; a blank or shared one gives the page no identity of its own.

scripted_findings.title: Pinch-zoom suppressed on 3 page(s)
scripted_findings.evidence: 3/11 crawled page(s) restrict zoom in the viewport meta tag, failing WCAG 1.4.4 (Resize Text). Examples: https://supercell.com/clashofclans-gift/$language$ sets user-scalable=no; https://supercell.com/clashofclans-gift/ar sets user-scalable=no; https://supercell.com/clashofclans-gift/ch sets user-scalable=no. iOS Safari has ignored these directives since iOS 10, so the impact falls on Android Chrome and other browsers that still honour them.

scripted_findings.title: 1 linked page(s) are broken
scripted_findings.evidence: https://supercell.com/google35ef817f8c8d3b22: HTTP 404 (listed in the sitemap). These URLs were reached from the homepage or the sitemap, so a crawler and a visitor both arrive at an error instead of the page.

scripted_findings.title: 1 page(s) answer HTTP 200 with a not-found page
scripted_findings.evidence: https://supercell.com/404: 'Page not found × Supercell'. A 200 tells crawlers the page exists, so the error text is indexed as the page's content and the real page, if any, is never looked for.

scripted_findings.title: No h1 heading on 7 page(s)
scripted_findings.evidence: 7/11 pages contain no h1 element at all. Examples: ['https://supercell.com/clashofclans-gift', 'https://supercell.com/brawlstars-gift', 'https://supercell.com/clashroyale-gift', 'https://supercell.com/hayday-gift']. Extractors and assistants use the top heading to decide what a page is about.

scripted_findings.title: No structured data on 2 significant page(s)
scripted_findings.evidence: 2/11 crawled pages of type ['about', 'home'] contain no JSON-LD. Structured data is read by the indexing crawlers that build the search index assistants query, and it states a fact with a type attached. Examples: ['https://supercell.com/', 'https://supercell.com/en/about-us']
